text.p: The following are the main stories from Wedenesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two experts of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation are lecturing Albanian bankers, police and auditors on money laundering and alleged pyramid schemes, which are reported to be proliferating here.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha has set up an anti-smuggling group with teams from government institutions to halt the crippling effects of smuggling on the country's finances.
- An Italian anti-Mafia commission will visit Albania on December 16 to coordinate methods to fight Italian-Albanian organized crime.

- The United Right of Shkoder, a rightist coalition between the Natianal Front and Monarchy Party, which won the mayorship of the key town of Shkoder, wants president Sali Berisha to step down, claiming he has been in power too long. The coalition called for new elections in 1997, a referendum on the form of government and the approval of a new constitution.
- Rexhep Mejdani, secretary general of the key opposition Socialist Party, is in Washington and is expected to meet top U.S. officials.

- The paper comments that Tirana's support of Serbia's Zajedno opposition is irrational because the the latter's stand on the issue of rights of ethnic Albanians in Serbia is worse than that of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
- Albanian banks will reduce loan and foreign exchange facilities ahead of their planned privatisation to reduce the risk of bad debts.
- The Silva company, which has just received a shipment of heavy machinery worth $4 million, plans to produce four million tonnes of bitumen from its bitumen sand concession in 1997.
- Women workers of a garments factory which has been privatised by the management will protest in front of the presidential office on Wednesday.

- Albanian Interior Minister Halit Shamata denied reports of money laundering in Albania. He said the coordination of joint patrols with Italy in the Adriatic would stop the flow of would-be-immigrants.
- Bashkim Kopliku, the head of Parliament's economic commission, says he wants banks to be privatised as soon as possible instead of restructuring them to increase their value.
- Lenient court verdicts are contributing to a rise in crime, according to a study by the prosecutor's office.
- An earthquake measuring 4.5 on the Richter scale shook Tirana last night but there was no damage.
- Anti-smuggling officials have seized Persian carpets with a value of $120,000 that had been declared as car tires and toys.
